[1/4] Plan Keystone asset-pack mode for foundry

impact_assessment.why: The user asked whether foundry can become a Keystone asset pipeline; foundry currently emits game-rule JSON only, while Keystone games need file-backed meshes, textures, materials and prefabs.
impact_assessment.benefits: One deterministic asset pack format with digests, dependency order and a runtime proof through Keystone's real AssetRegistry; Keystone and the games stay read-only.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new pack schema and CLI; dependency: Keystone only for the optional runtime proof; concurrency: none; state: baseline pack under packs/keystone/starter plus target manifest and ledger
impact_assessment.mitigation: Generate with stdlib (OBJ, PNG, KPREFAB), validate hashes and dependencies, load/instantiate through Keystone, run the foundry suite and aikit check.

[1/4] Inventory and classify every project in the portfolio

impact_assessment.why: The user asked to continue analyzing the projects after the first target and Keystone slices; the remaining playable projects were not yet registered in foundry.
impact_assessment.benefits: A complete portfolio map that separates game/content targets from tools, science and apps, backed by source-derived content surfaces rather than guesses.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: registry grows to 14 targets plus the Keystone engine; dependency: stdlib only for adapters; concurrency: none; state: four new adapters and manifests
impact_assessment.mitigation: Read each candidate project's README and source, add only targets with authored content surfaces, validate counts, run the suite and aikit check.
